title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
Given `n` non-negative integers `height` representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is `1`, compute how much total rainwater can be trapped between the bars after raining.

Water trapped above bar `i` is bounded by the shorter of the tallest bar to its left and the tallest bar to its right.
hints: At any index i, the water level is min(maxLeft[i], maxRight[i]), contributing max(0, waterLevel - height[i]) units of water.
You can eliminate the O(n) prefix/suffix arrays by maintaining two converging pointers left and right along with running maxima leftMax and rightMax.

Whenever height[left] <= height[right], the limiting wall for left is guaranteed to be leftMax (since there is a bar at least as tall on the right), so you can safely accumulate water at left and advance it.

examples.explanation: Water pools between the elevation peaks for a total of 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 6 units.
The bars form pockets holding 2 + 4 + 1 + 2 = 9 units of water.
A strictly increasing elevation map has no right boundary lower than a left wall, so 0 units of water are trapped.
